subject: physics
question_text: Give the expression for the excess pressure in a liquid drop. Mention the terms in the expression.

mark_split.label: The terms ΔP, T and r

verification.note: Asked in TS Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I, March 2017 (Q6) and March 2023 (Q6) — Section A, 2 marks each time. The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: a liquid drop is liquid throughout and meets the air at ONE surface, so the excess pressure is ΔP = 2T/r. The same 2T/r holds for an air bubble inside a liquid, which also has one liquid surface; a soap bubble in air has TWO surfaces and gives 4T/r. This question also asks for the meaning of each term, so ΔP, T and r must each be named.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.margin_note: First mark. Say the drop has one liquid surface, then write 2T/r.
steps.why: The number of liquid surfaces fixes the numerator. One surface gives 2T/r; a soap bubble has two and gives 4T/r.
common_mistakes: Writing 4T/r, which belongs to a soap bubble with two surfaces.
Writing 2T/r² . The radius appears to the first power.

steps.memory_tip: A drop is liquid throughout, so it has one boundary with air: one surface, 2T/r.
